brief.title: Usage-based Billing & Invoicing Platform
business_goals: Transition from flat monthly rate to usage-based pricing per API call.
Automate usage reconciliation to scale beyond 400 customers and eliminate manual spreadsheet processes.
Provide customers with real-time visibility into their API usage (updated within minutes).
Accurately calculate tiered usage charges to ensure correct revenue recognition.
Implement customer usage alerts for spending caps (e.g., 80% notification).
Ensure invoices are generated and sent within 24 hours of the billing period closing.
Build a scalable and reliable metering pipeline capable of handling high volumes (e.g., 40 million API calls/month) without dropping events.
Automate dunning and failed-payment retry logic.
Reduce manual effort and resolve discrepancies between finance and engineering regarding billing numbers.

stakeholders.name: Laura Bennett
concerns: Correct calculation of tiered charges for revenue recognition
Timely invoice generation (within 24 hours of period close)
Seven years of invoice and usage data retention for tax and audit
Project live before fiscal year starts on July 1st

stakeholders.name: Chris Nakamura
concerns: Customers need real-time visibility into their usage
Customers need usage alerts (e.g., 80% spending cap notification)

stakeholders.name: Omar Haddad
concerns: Billing system must consume from existing Kafka topic for metering events
Metering pipeline must handle high volume (40M API calls/month) without dropping events

stakeholders.name: Grace Lindqvist
concerns: Invoices must be sent through Stripe (existing payment processor)
Automatic dunning and failed-payment retry logic

constraints: Billing system must consume usage events from an existing Kafka topic.
Invoices must be processed and sent via Stripe (existing payment processor).
Project must be live before the fiscal year starts on July 1st.
Project budget is capped at $400,000 (including Kafka and Stripe integration).
Seven years of invoice and usage data must be retained for tax and audit purposes.
Metering pipeline must handle high volume (e.g., 40 million API calls/month) without dropping events.
Customer usage visibility must be updated within a few minutes.
out_of_scope: Building a second metering layer (must use existing Kafka topic).
Multi-currency billing (only USD invoicing in this phase).

requirements.statement: The system shall support usage-based pricing per API call.
requirements.evidence: Right now we bill customers on a flat monthly rate, but we're moving to usage-based pricing per API call

requirements.statement: The system shall automate usage reconciliation.
requirements.evidence: finance is currently reconciling usage in spreadsheets pulled from our logs — it doesn't scale past our current 400 customers.

requirements.statement: The system shall scale beyond 400 customers.
requirements.evidence: finance is currently reconciling usage in spreadsheets pulled from our logs — it doesn't scale past our current 400 customers.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide customers with visibility into their API usage.
requirements.evidence: Customers need real-time visibility into their own usage — API calls consumed so far this billing period

requirements.statement: The system shall update customer API usage visibility within a few minutes.
requirements.evidence: ideally updated within a few minutes, not just at month end.

requirements.statement: The system shall consume metering events from the existing Kafka topic.
requirements.evidence: We already emit metering events to a Kafka topic — the billing system needs to consume from that topic rather than us building a second metering layer.

requirements.statement: The system shall calculate tiered usage charges.
requirements.evidence: Each customer has a contracted rate per thousand API calls, and some have tiered pricing — the first 100,000 calls at one rate, everything above at a lower rate. The system has to calculate tiered charges correctly

requirements.statement: The system shall accurately calculate usage charges.
requirements.evidence: The system has to calculate tiered charges correctly, we cannot get this wrong, it directly hits revenue recognition.

requirements.statement: The system shall provide customer usage alerts.
requirements.evidence: We also want usage alerts — ideally customers get notified by email when they hit 80% of any spending cap they've set for themselves.

requirements.statement: The system shall notify customers by email when they reach 80% of their spending cap.
requirements.evidence: ideally customers get notified by email when they hit 80% of any spending cap they've set for themselves.

requirements.statement: The system shall send invoices through Stripe.
requirements.evidence: Invoices need to go out through Stripe, since that's our existing payment processor and customers already have cards on file there — we are not switching payment processors as part of this.

requirements.statement: The system shall generate and send invoices within 24 hours of the billing period closing.
requirements.evidence: Invoices must be generated and sent within 24 hours of the billing period closing.

requirements.statement: The metering pipeline shall handle 40 million API calls per month.
requirements.evidence: For scale, our biggest customer alone generates about 40 million API calls a month. The metering pipeline needs to handle that volume

requirements.statement: The metering pipeline shall not drop events.
requirements.evidence: The metering pipeline needs to handle that volume without dropping events — we can't have billing disputes because we undercounted someone's usage.

requirements.statement: The system shall automate dunning logic.
requirements.evidence: Dunning and failed-payment retry logic should ideally be automatic

requirements.statement: The system shall automate failed-payment retry logic.
requirements.evidence: Dunning and failed-payment retry logic should ideally be automatic

requirements.statement: The system shall retry a failed card three times over a week.
requirements.evidence: retry a failed card three times over a week before flagging the account to a human.

requirements.statement: The system shall retain invoice and usage data for seven years.
requirements.evidence: We need seven years of invoice and usage data retained for tax and audit purposes, that's a hard finance requirement, not optional.

requirements.statement: The system shall comply with tax and audit data retention requirements.
requirements.evidence: We need seven years of invoice and usage data retained for tax and audit purposes, that's a hard finance requirement, not optional.

requirements.evidence: This needs to be live before our fiscal year starts on July 1st

epics.title: Usage Metering & Processing
epics.goal: Accurately capture and process all API usage events to support usage-based billing.

epics.title: Usage-Based Pricing & Calculation
epics.goal: Implement flexible pricing models and accurately calculate charges based on processed usage data.

epics.title: Customer Usage Visibility
epics.goal: Provide customers with transparent and near real-time access to their API usage data.

epics.title: Invoicing & Billing Automation
epics.goal: Automate the generation and delivery of accurate invoices to customers.

epics.title: Customer Spending Alerts
epics.goal: Proactively notify customers about their usage to help them manage costs.

epics.title: Dunning & Payment Recovery
epics.goal: Automate the process of recovering failed payments and managing overdue accounts.

epics.title: Data Retention & Compliance
epics.goal: Ensure all billing and usage data is stored securely and compliantly for required periods.

stories.title: Implement Basic Metering Pipeline for Event Ingestion and Storage
stories.i_want: to reliably consume API usage events from Kafka and store them
stories.so_that: all customer API calls are accurately recorded for subsequent billing calculations

acceptance_criteria.given: a stream of API usage events on the existing Kafka topic
acceptance_criteria.when: the metering pipeline processes these events
acceptance_criteria.then: all events are captured and persisted in the system's data store, and are available for downstream billing calculations

acceptance_criteria.given: the metering pipeline is processing events
acceptance_criteria.when: a new API usage event is sent to Kafka
acceptance_criteria.then: the event is ingested and stored without loss in this basic implementation

stories.notes: This story focuses on the initial reliable consumption and storage of events. Scalability (R-013) and robust event guarantees (R-014) will be addressed in separate non-functional requirement stories or epics. The stored data will be made available for downstream billing calculations.

stories.title: Automate Usage Reconciliation
stories.i_want: the system to automatically reconcile processed usage data
stories.so_that: manual spreadsheet processes are eliminated and billing data is accurate

acceptance_criteria.given: processed API usage data for a billing period is available
acceptance_criteria.when: the reconciliation process runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the system provides a report detailing the consistency and completeness of the usage data

acceptance_criteria.given: a discrepancy is detected during reconciliation
acceptance_criteria.when: the system identifies the issue
acceptance_criteria.then: it logs the discrepancy with relevant details and flags it for review

stories.title: Configure Tiered Usage-Based Pricing
stories.i_want: to configure tiered usage-based pricing per API call
stories.so_that: we can implement flexible pricing strategies and accurately charge customers based on their consumption

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's processed API usage for a billing period
acceptance_criteria.when: the system calculates the charges
acceptance_criteria.then: the system applies the defined tiered pricing model and calculates the total charge

acceptance_criteria.given: a pricing tier structure (e.g., 0-1M calls at $X, 1M+ calls at $Y) and a customer's usage of 1.5M calls
acceptance_criteria.when: the system calculates the charge
acceptance_criteria.then: the system calculates the total charge as (1M * $X) + (0.5M * $Y)

stories.title: Display Real-time Customer Usage
stories.i_want: to view my API usage in near real-time
stories.so_that: I can monitor my consumption and understand my current billing status

acceptance_criteria.given: I am logged into my customer portal
acceptance_criteria.when: I navigate to the usage dashboard
acceptance_criteria.then: I see my API usage data updated within a few minutes of actual usage

acceptance_criteria.given: I have made recent API calls
acceptance_criteria.when: I refresh my usage dashboard
acceptance_criteria.then: the displayed usage reflects those calls within minutes

stories.notes: This story focuses on the functional display of near real-time usage. Scalability beyond 400 customers (R-003) is an architectural concern and will be addressed through overall system design and performance testing, not within this specific story.

stories.title: Configure Customer Spending Caps & Alerts
stories.i_want: to set spending caps and configure usage alert thresholds for customers
stories.so_that: customers can be proactively notified about their consumption

acceptance_criteria.given: I am configuring a customer's billing settings
acceptance_criteria.when: I set a spending cap of $1000 for the customer
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays and confirms the spending cap is saved for that customer

acceptance_criteria.given: I want to notify a customer at 80% of their spending cap
acceptance_criteria.when: I configure an alert threshold of 80%
acceptance_criteria.then: the system displays and confirms the 80% alert threshold is saved for that customer

stories.title: Notify Customers of Usage Thresholds
stories.i_want: to receive email notifications when my API usage approaches my spending cap
stories.so_that: I can manage my costs and avoid unexpected overages

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer has an 80% spending cap alert configured
acceptance_criteria.when: their usage reaches 80% of that cap
acceptance_criteria.then: the system automatically sends an email notification to the customer

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer receives an 80% usage alert
acceptance_criteria.when: they check their email
acceptance_criteria.then: the email clearly states their current usage, the cap, and the percentage reached

stories.notes: This story depends on S-001 (usage data ingestion), S-003 (usage calculation), and a separate story for 'Configure Customer Spending Caps and Alert Rules' (S-005, not yet defined) being completed or sufficiently advanced.

stories.title: Generate Invoices and Initiate Sending via Stripe
stories.i_want: the system to automatically generate invoices and initiate sending them through Stripe
stories.so_that: the billing process is efficient and customers receive timely invoices

acceptance_criteria.given: a billing period has closed and processed usage data is available for a customer
acceptance_criteria.when: the invoice generation process is triggered for that customer
acceptance_criteria.then: the system creates an accurate invoice document based on their usage and calculated charges

acceptance_criteria.given: an accurate invoice document has been generated for a customer
acceptance_criteria.when: the system attempts to send the invoice via Stripe
acceptance_criteria.then: the system successfully transmits the invoice data to Stripe for delivery

stories.notes: This story depends on S-001 (usage data ingestion) and S-003 (pricing calculation). This story covers the capability to generate and initiate sending invoices. The full automation and scheduling to meet the 24-hour SLA (R-012) may require additional scheduling and monitoring stories.

stories.title: Implement Initial Automated Dunning Action (e.g., First Reminder)
stories.i_want: the system to automate the first step of dunning logic
stories.so_that: overdue payments are pursued consistently and efficiently with an initial reminder

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's invoice is 7 days overdue
acceptance_criteria.when: the dunning process runs
acceptance_criteria.then: the system automatically sends a predefined 'first overdue' email reminder to the customer

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's payment fails for an invoice
acceptance_criteria.when: the system detects the failed payment
acceptance_criteria.then: it flags the invoice as requiring dunning action (e.g., for the first reminder)

stories.notes: This story depends on S-007 (invoice generation) and a payment processing system (to detect failed payments). Further dunning steps will require additional stories.

stories.title: Implement Automated Failed Payment Retry Logic
stories.i_want: the system to automatically retry failed payments
stories.so_that: revenue recovery is maximized and manual follow-up is reduced

acceptance_criteria.given: a customer's credit card payment fails for an invoice
acceptance_criteria.when: the system detects the failure
acceptance_criteria.then: it automatically schedules and attempts to retry the card three times over a week, with appropriate delays

acceptance_criteria.given: a payment retry sequence is completed without success after three attempts
acceptance_criteria.when: the system finishes the retries
acceptance_criteria.then: it marks the invoice as uncollectible via automated retries and flags the account for further review or dunning escalation

stories.notes: This story depends on the integration with a payment gateway (e.g., Stripe) to process payments and report failures.

stories.title: Establish Data Retention Mechanism for New Billing Data
stories.i_want: the system to store all new invoice and usage data in a manner that supports seven-year retention
stories.so_that: we can comply with tax and audit requirements for newly generated data

acceptance_criteria.given: new invoice and usage data is generated
acceptance_criteria.when: the data is stored by the system
acceptance_criteria.then: it is stored in a designated long-term storage solution configured for a minimum of seven years retention

acceptance_criteria.given: an audit request for a specific invoice or usage record generated after this feature is live
acceptance_criteria.when: the system is queried for that record
acceptance_criteria.then: it successfully retrieves the requested invoice or usage data from the long-term storage

stories.notes: This story focuses on establishing the retention mechanism for *new* data. Strategies for migrating or archiving *existing* historical data, and complex retrieval mechanisms for very large datasets, may require additional stories.

gaps.description: The brief mentions a goal to 'Reduce manual effort and resolve discrepancies between finance and engineering regarding billing numbers.' While automation and accurate calculation are covered, there's no explicit requirement or backlog item addressing the *resolution* mechanism for discrepancies or how to build trust between teams beyond just accurate numbers.
gaps.suggested_question: How will the system specifically help resolve discrepancies between finance and engineering, beyond just providing accurate numbers? Are there specific reporting or reconciliation features needed for this?

gaps.description: Requirement R-003 states the system shall scale beyond 400 customers. While S-001 is foundational, no specific backlog item explicitly addresses or plans for this non-functional requirement for customer scaling.
gaps.suggested_question: How will the backlog ensure that the system is designed and tested to scale beyond 400 customers, as per R-003?

gaps.description: Requirement R-013 specifies the metering pipeline must handle 40 million API calls per month. S-001 covers basic ingestion but doesn't explicitly address this high-volume non-functional requirement.
gaps.suggested_question: How will the backlog ensure the metering pipeline is built to handle 40 million API calls per month without performance degradation, as required by R-013?

gaps.description: Requirement R-014 states the metering pipeline shall not drop events. S-001 covers basic ingestion but doesn't explicitly address this critical reliability non-functional requirement.
gaps.suggested_question: What specific tasks or design considerations in the backlog will ensure the metering pipeline does not drop events, as required by R-014?

gaps.description: Requirement R-015 calls for automating dunning logic, but backlog item S-008 specifies 'Initial Automated Dunning Action (e.g., First Reminder)'. This suggests a partial implementation, which might not fully satisfy the broader requirement for comprehensive 'dunning logic'.
gaps.suggested_question: Does 'Initial Automated Dunning Action' in S-008 fully cover the scope of 'automate dunning logic' as per R-015, or are further dunning steps planned for a later phase?

gaps.description: Requirement R-018 and Laura's concern mention retaining invoice and usage data for seven years. Backlog item S-010 specifies 'Establish Data Retention Mechanism for New Billing Data'. It's unclear if existing historical data also needs to be migrated or handled for retention.
gaps.suggested_question: Does S-010 only cover data retention for newly generated billing data, or does it also include a plan for retaining existing historical invoice and usage data as implied by Laura's concern?

gaps.description: Requirement R-020 states the project must be live before July 1st. This is a critical project constraint/non-functional requirement but is not reflected in any backlog item.
gaps.suggested_question: How will the project timeline constraint (R-020: live before July 1st) be managed and tracked within the backlog or project plan?

gaps.description: Requirement R-021 states the project budget is capped at $400,000. This is a critical project constraint/non-functional requirement but is not reflected in any backlog item.
gaps.suggested_question: How will the project budget constraint (R-021: capped at $400,000) be managed and tracked against the backlog items?

gaps.coverage_note: The backlog provides good coverage for most functional requirements derived from the brief's business goals, addressing key areas like usage-based pricing, reconciliation, customer visibility, alerts, invoicing, and basic dunning/retry logic. However, there are significant gaps in covering critical non-functional requirements related to scalability (customer count, metering volume, event reliability), and project-level constraints (timeline, budget). Additionally, some backlog items are ambiguously scoped, potentially leading to incomplete fulfillment of requirements, and one high-level business goal regarding discrepancy resolution is not fully translated into actionable requirements or backlog items.
